title: Empty State Message
prompt: A React list view needs empty-state copy. Write a helper that returns "No results" when count is 0 and an empty string when count is greater than 0.

explanation.beginner:
Example: emptyStateMessage(0) produces "No results". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “hides empty state for results”: input [3] produces "". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “hides empty state for results”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
